COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
C528 No.706 of 2026
Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. V.D. Bisen, Advocate for the 
applicant. 
2. Applicant is aggrieved by the orders 
dated 17.05.2025 and 23.03.2026, whereby 
his application seeking setting aside of the 
ex-parte order has been rejected, and the 
Criminal Revision preferred thereagainst has 
also been dismissed.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant 
submits that no notice of the aforesaid 
proceedings was ever duly served upon the 
applicant. It is contended that this fact has 
been specifically averred in the application 
filed under Order IX Rule 13 C.P.C. 
However, the Revisional Court, while 
dismissing the revision, has erroneously 
observed that the applicant had not stated 
the said fact in his affidavit, despite the 
same having been clearly pleaded in the 
application under Order IX Rule 13 C.P.C. It 
is further submitted that in the event the 
impugned orders are not set aside and the 
applicant is not afforded an opportunity to 
cross-examine the respondent and to 
adduce evidence in support of his case, the 
applicant shall suffer irreparable loss and 
grave prejudice.
4. Issue notice to the respondent, 
returnable at an early date.
5. List the matter after receipt of the 
service report. 
6. Considering the submissions advanced 
by learned counsel for the applicant, it is 
directed that, till the next date of listing, 
further proceedings of Misc. Criminal Case 
No.67 of 2025, pending before the Court of  learned Additional Principal Judge, Family 
Court, Haldwani, District Nainital, shall 
remain stayed.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 
 17.04.2026
Arpan

UKHC010059712026
C528/706/2026
Aditya Malik --Applicant
 Versus
Shivangi Tomar --Respondent
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Mr. V.D. Bisen, learned counsel for the 
applicant. 
2. Mr. Pankaj Kumar Sharma, learned 
counsel for the respondent. 
3. The parties are present and earlier both 
of them appeared before the Counsellor for 
their Counselling. The Counsellor’s report 
dated 24.07.2026 is also on record. 
4. I perused the Counsellor’s report, on 
perusal of which, it reveals that before the 
Counsellor both of them were agreed for 
reunion of their relationship and to live 
together and to give due regard to each 
other. The written undertakings are also the 
part of the Counsellor’s report. 
5. Today the respondent is present with 
her mother.
6. On perusal of the report and after 
interaction it reveals that both of them are 
now fighting only for minor issues though 
the husband is always ready for resolving the 
matrimonial dispute and want to live 
together. He also filed a petition for the 
restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 
of Hindu Marriage Act in March 2025 but the 
respondent-wife chooses to approach the 
police authorities. 7. The report further reveals that there is 
lot of interference of their family members 
and there is also a communication gap in 
between both of them and it is apprised that 
only for six weeks they lived together. 
8. Put up this matter on 24.08.2026.
9. Interim order is made absolute. 
10. In the meantime, the parties may think 
over it and then come up with the fresh 
proposal and it is also advised to the family 
members of both the parties not to interfere 
in between both of them so that both of them 
in the meantime think over it and still their 
family members want to intervene they only 
intervene to settle their matrimonial issues 
amicably. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 03.08.2026
Arti
